_note: The Story of Prophet Ilyas (Elijah), drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs as-Saffat and al-An'am). Ilyas, of the house of Harun, was sent to a people who worshipped the idol Baʿl; the Qur'an records his call, their denial, and the peace left upon him among later generations. Verse text resolves from the loaded Qur'an. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: Among the Messengers
events.summary: 'And indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers.' The Qur'an numbers him among the sent prophets, and elsewhere names him with Zakariyya, Yahya, and Isa among the righteous — one guidance carried by many messengers to one straying people.
events.why: Ilyas is placed squarely within the single chain of prophethood: not a new religion but the same message, sent again to a nation that had turned from it.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “Indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers” (as-Saffat 37:123).
Schematic diagram of the setting — the town of Baʿl to which Ilyas was sent.

events.title: The Call Against Baʿl
events.summary: He said to his people, 'Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Baʿl and leave the best of creators — Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers?' He named their idol and set against it the one truth: that the Creator alone deserves worship, as He did for their fathers before them.
events.why: Ilyas confronts the specific idol of his people by name, exposing the folly of praying to a made thing while forsaking the Maker — the same argument every prophet brings against every false god.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “Do you call upon Baʿl and leave the best of creators?” (as-Saffat 37:125).
Schematic diagram of the setting — The Call Against Baʿl.

events.title: They Denied Him
events.summary: 'And they denied him, so indeed, they will be brought [for punishment], except the chosen servants of Allah.' His people rejected the call, and the Qur'an records their coming reckoning — save only those sincere servants of Allah whom the warning reached and moved.
events.why: The denial is met with a just consequence, but the exception is left standing: the sincere are spared. Rejection is never total, and mercy always keeps a door for the few who truly worship.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “Except the chosen servants of Allah” (as-Saffat 37:128).
Schematic diagram of the setting — They Denied Him.

events.title: Peace Upon Ilyas
events.summary: 'And We left for him [favourable mention] among later generations: Peace upon Ilyas. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.' Though his people turned away, Allah preserved his honour and greeting of peace on the tongues of all who came after.
events.why: The prophet rejected by his own is crowned by his Lord: a lasting name, a greeting of peace, and the seal of being 'of Our believing servants' — proof that the doer of good is never the loser, whatever his people do.

media.caption: Schematic diagram of the setting — Peace Upon Ilyas.

paths.title: The Arc of Ilyas
paths.blurb: The messenger of the house of Harun — his place among the prophets, his call against the idol Baʿl, his people's denial, and the peace left upon him among later generations.

paths.title: The Call and the Answer
paths.blurb: One idol named, one truth proclaimed, and two answers — a people's denial and a Lord's lasting peace.
